title: AirMPA: A Meteorology-to-Pollution Adapter for Global Air Quality Forecasting
claim: Decoupling meteorology from pollutant forecasting via a specialized attention block enables stable, boundary-continuous autoregressive rollout from external forecasts.
layout: 3 panels: wide top overview, bottom-left block detail, bottom-right rollout timeline
description: A dense three-panel architecture figure with pastel-colored boxes and chevron headers. Panel (a), across the top, flows left to right: a Features Input column showing globe maps of pollutant concentration, emissions and meteorology at t-24, t-12 and t0, plus time features. These feed a Model Architecture stage of rearrange, cube embedding, a stack of AirMPA blocks (x20), patch expansion and a dual-branch fusion with softmax and a history skip connection. The flow ends at a stacked world-map concentration output and a Training Stage column with three cubes, loss formulas and red arrows. Panel (b), bottom left, shows two transformer block diagrams (MHA and SW-MHA) plus a colored-grid mask illustration and a feature map with green and red borders. Panel (c), bottom right, shows a timeline from t0 to 120 h with emissions, meteorology (FuXi) and CAMS rows feeding AirMPA rollout steps, with blue boxes for initial inputs and red boxes for rollout predictions.
caption: AirMPA architecture. (a) Overview of the AirMPA architecture and data flow. (b) Illustration of the zonal release attention mechanism, which mitigates the artificial discontinuity at the global longitude boundary. (c) Autoregressive inference pipeline for multi-step pollutant forecasting.
abstract: Accurate real-time forecasting of atmospheric pollutants is essential for reducing exposure risks and improving public health. Traditional numerical forecasting systems suffer from incomplete parameterizations, uncertain inputs, and high computational cost. Existing deep learning approaches improve efficiency, but often entangle meteorological and pollutant variables within unified forecasting frameworks, limiting flexibility and pollutant-specific representation learning. To address these challenges, we propose AirMPA, a decoupled autoregressive framework for meteorology-to-pollution forecasting. AirMPA predicts 13 atmospheric pollutants at 0.4Â° spatial resolution and 12-h temporal resolution using meteorological fields, emission priors, and historical pollutant concentrations. The model is built on an improved Swin-Transformer architecture with zonal release attention and dual-branch fusion, enabling more effective modeling of global transport continuity and heterogeneous pollutant dynamics. During training, AirMPA uses the fifth-generation atmospheric reanalysis from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ERA5) as meteorological forcing, while during inference it directly ingests forecast fields from external meteorological models, enabling stable autoregressive prediction up to 5 days ahead. Experiments show that AirMPA consistently outperforms Aurora and surpasses the Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service (CAMS) in approximately 90% of pollutant-lead-time evaluation cases over the 5-day forecast horizon, while outperforming CAMS on all variables beyond 48 h. These results demonstrate the potential of decoupled meteorology-to-pollution forecasting for global air quality prediction.
